test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

We should plan our actions __judiciously__ before going to war.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Irrational**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"judiciously"** means using or showing good judgment, wise, or sensible. (विवेकपूर्ण तरीके से)

 
 
• **Example:** We need to spend our money judiciously to make sure we don't run out before the end of the month.
 
 
 
• **"Irrational"** refers to a lack of reason or logic; it means not based on reason or clear thinking. (अतार्किक)
 
 
• **Example:** His fear of spiders is completely irrational.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **"judiciously"** is **"irrational"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Irrational**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Irreverent** (असम्मानजनक): Showing a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously.

 
 
• **Example:** His irreverent comments about the ceremony shocked everyone.
 
 
 
• **Irrelevant** (अप्रासंगिक): Not connected with or relevant to something.
 
 
• **Example:** The evidence presented in court was deemed irrelevant to the case.
 
 
 
• **Irritatingly** (चिड़चिड़ेपन से): In a manner that causes irritation or annoyance.
 
 
• **Example:** She tapped her pen irritatingly on the desk throughout the meeting.
